claims.text: The superconducting transition temperature in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by the degree of local chemical ordering.
Moderate short-range chemical ordering optimizes electron-phonon coupling.
Excessive atomic disorder enhances electron scattering.
Disorder-enhanced electron scattering suppresses Cooper-pair formation.
Rapid solidification produces an as-cast alloy with a uniform but highly disordered atomic distribution.
Controlled annealing can induce moderate short-range chemical ordering.
Controlled annealing can induce moderate short-range ordering without macroscopic phase separation.
Annealing promotes limited atomic rearrangements.
Limited atomic rearrangements generate local regions of chemical order.
Local regions of chemical order increase the local density of states near the Fermi level.
An increased local density of states near the Fermi level enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling facilitates Cooper-pair formation.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling raises the superconducting transition temperature.
Optimally annealed samples will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than unannealed samples.
Optimally annealed samples will show stronger electron-phonon coupling signals than unannealed samples.
The proposed ordering effect applies only to high-entropy superconducting alloys dominated by electron-phonon pairing.
Ordering beyond a moderate degree may reduce superconductivity.
Phase separation may reduce superconductivity.
Materials with non-electron-phonon pairing mechanisms may not exhibit the proposed ordering dependence.
The as-cast baseline has a fully random atomic distribution.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires successful induction of moderate short-range ordering, but the falsification rule treats ordering that is too low to have an effect as falsification. Failure to achieve the intended mediator would instead make the test inconclusive.

Phase separation and excessive ordering are stated to be outside the proposed valid regime, yet a phase-separated, excessively ordered sample with no Tc improvement is also treated as falsifying the hypothesis.
